frontier.hypothesis: F8 — motion_Close is an escalation candidate and the ladder's remaining rungs (rederive, synthesis) are the only untried modalities; every sanctioned axis this ledger has measured is now dead.
frontier.mechanism: Three independent frozen-toolchain mechanisms account for all 13 residual points: H1 (REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE=16 ⇒ frame >= 32 vs the target's 16, census of 854 call-making functions), F5 (ascending first-free hard-reg scan, no MIPS REG_ALLOC_ORDER ⇒ $v0 not $t0), F7 (block-local scheduling ⇒ descending saves, and a non-empty block ⇒ a filled delay slot). Each is a 'no C input to this compiler produces these bytes' argument, not a 'the search has not found it' argument, and each now carries a corpus measurement rather than a narrative.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT self-dispose — exhaustion is the driver's call. What is left for a session is the escalation packet's shape, and it is now fully determined: the canonical-asm gate FAILS on measurement (scan_hand_coded tier LOW 0/8, both this function and its sibling), and no coercion/spelling family has an in-hand SOTN-master precedent, so under the owner's 2026-07-27 standing auto-ruling a both-gates-fail entry is the terminal disposition whenever the driver routes this to `escalation`. A rederive/synthesis session should spend itself on the ONE thing not yet tried: reconstructing the function from the sibling func_80083794's shape (they are the same crt0 open/close pair and differ only in the guard polarity and the D_800A2668 store), to see whether a whole-file/TU-level change — not a body-level one — moves any of the three mechanisms.

frontier.hypothesis: F9 (new, low value but genuinely untried) — the 16-byte outgoing-arg area H1 attributes to REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE could be avoided if the indirect call were not a C-level call at all in the ORIGINAL source either.
frontier.mechanism: H1's census showed the only two sub-16 arg-area functions in the build are motion_Close and func_80083794, both of which get there because their jalr is inline asm (an __asm__ block never sets current_function_outgoing_args_size). That is a statement about OUR build. The complementary question — what C construct, if any, makes gcc-2.7.2 emit a jalr without reserving the arg area — has never been probed directly; the ledger inferred it from the census rather than from the backend.
frontier.next_probe: Read mips.c/function.c for every path that sets current_function_outgoing_args_size and check whether ANY of them can be reached with a call expression (not an asm) that yields zero — e.g. a call through a pointer with a prototype gcc treats specially, or -mno-abicalls interactions. Expected outcome is a fourth structural kill, which is worth having explicitly: it converts H1 from 'census says no function does this' into 'the backend cannot do this', which is the stronger claim an escalation should carry.

frontier.hypothesis: F4b (carried forward, now purely cosmetic) — reach floor 13 with a wrap depth below 3.
frontier.mechanism: The floor-13 form's only construct is a THREE-level do{}while(0) wrap around p's initialiser, which wins p $s0 by loop-depth reference weighting (p 10 weighted refs / live_length 8 = 37500 vs count's 34285). Depths 1 and 2 are measured insufficient (both 20) and depths 4-6 buy nothing, so the device is minimal for THIS body — but a body reaching 13 with a lighter device would be strictly better to put in front of a reviewer.
frontier.next_probe: Only worth spending time on if a future session is preparing a submission, which cannot happen while H1 stands (distance 0 is unreachable, so no candidate-ready is possible). Sweep bodies that lengthen count's live range without adding a count reference — an intervening real computation the target also performs — and measure score AND the allocno table (BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1). Success criterion is score 13 at wrap depth < 3, not a lower score.
